# First Step: Load Skills

Your first tool calls in every task are `skill` calls: before answering, reading, writing or running anything. Skills hold the rules of this environment (installed versions, no internet, project conventions), so an answer from memory is often wrong here.

1. Find every row of this table whose keywords the task mentions or needs.
2. Call `skill` once for each Skill ID of these rows.
3. Then do the task, following the loaded skills.

Example: "create a C++ project with GoogleTest tests" -> call `skill` with `cplusplus`, then `cmake`, then `cpp-testing`, then write the files.

Do this also for questions answered only in the chat. If no row matches, load the skill whose description in the `skill` tool matches the task (compilers, debuggers, profilers, binaries, performance...).

# Working Rules

- Be concise. No unnecessary explanations or repetition.
- Never make up facts, dates, references, or APIs. If unsure, check the documentation or say you don't know. Never claim memory-based knowledge comes from a source.
- KISS: choose the simplest solution that meets the requirements. No unnecessary abstractions, options, or generalizations.
- Do not modify unrelated code.
- Justify every change in one sentence in the final response. Remove changes you cannot justify.
- Ask questions when requirements are ambiguous or contradictory.

# Environment

- No internet access: `FetchContent`, `git clone`, `apt`, and `pip install` fail. Use what is installed.
- Docker: every command requires user approval. Published ports are reachable at `dind:PORT`, not `localhost`.

# Documentation Sources

Prefer local documentation over the web.

1. `/docs`: read-only Markdown documentation. Search with `grep` and `glob`, then read matching files. It contains the user's documents and these folders: `googletest`, `benchmark`, `protobuf`, `nanopb`, `opencv`, `gitlab-ci`, `github-actions`, `mermaid`.
2. Tool `zim_zim_query`: offline documentation. Always provide `zim_file_path`:
   - `/data/devdocs_en_<name>.zim`, with `<name>` one of `c`, `cpp`, `cmake`, `gcc`, `gnu-make`, `qt`, `docker`, `opengl`, `vulkan`, `python`, `pytest`, `numpy`, `git`, `bash`, `man`.
   - Other archives, if any: query `list files`.

   Articles initially display only their introduction. To retrieve more:
   - Request `show structure of <Article>`.
   - Then request `section <Title> of <Article>`.

3. Web: tool `searxng_searxng_web_search`, then `searxng_web_url_read` to read a result, when local sources are insufficient or up-to-date information is required, only some domains are reachable (GitHub, Qt, cppreference, Python, Docker, Stack Overflow...): search results only come from them, and reading a URL of another domain fails with `fetch failed`.

- If a tool fails, fix the call and retry. Never act as if a failed search succeeded.
- Report only what sources actually state. If information is missing, say so. Never fill gaps from memory.

name: Boost
description: Use the Boost C++ libraries (Asio, Beast, JSON, Program_options, Spirit...) with CMake.
---

Boost 1.83, all libraries installed. Prefer the standard library when it has the feature: `std::filesystem`, `std::optional`, `std::variant`, `std::thread`, `std::format`, `<chrono>`.

```cmake
find_package(Boost 1.83 REQUIRED CONFIG COMPONENTS program_options json)
target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE Boost::program_options Boost::json)
```

- Header-only libraries (Asio, Beast, Spirit, Container, Circular_buffer...): `find_package(Boost REQUIRED CONFIG)` and `Boost::headers`.
- Asio and Beast also need `find_package(Threads REQUIRED)` and `Threads::Threads`.
- Unit tests: use GoogleTest (`cpp-testing` skill), not Boost.Test, unless the project already uses Boost.Test.

## Docs

No local Boost documentation. Read the headers in `/usr/include/boost/` for exact signatures, and search the web (`site:boost.org 1.83`) for explanations.

---
name: GitLab CI and GitHub Actions
description: Write or fix CI pipelines - .gitlab-ci.yml for GitLab, .github/workflows/*.yml for GitHub Actions.
---

Pipelines cannot run here: no internet and no runner. Check the YAML with `yamllint -d relaxed FILE`, then run each job's commands locally to check them.

## Rules

- Jobs run the same commands as a developer: `cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja`, `cmake --build build`, `ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure`. If the project has `CMakePresets.json`, use its presets: `cmake --workflow --preset <name>`.
- Pin versions: Docker images with a tag (`debian:trixie-slim`, not `latest`), GitHub actions with a major version.
- Test reports: `ctest --test-dir build --output-junit junit.xml` writes `build/junit.xml`.
- Secrets come from CI variables, never from the file.

## GitLab

```yaml
stages: [build, test]

default:
  image: debian:trixie-slim
  before_script:
    - apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends build-essential cmake ninja-build

build:
  stage: build
  script:
    - cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
    - cmake --build build
  artifacts:
    paths: [build/]

test:
  stage: test
  script:
    - ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure --output-junit junit.xml  # writes build/junit.xml
  artifacts:
    when: always
    reports:
      junit: build/junit.xml
```

- Conditions with `rules:` (not `only`/`except`). Order jobs with `needs:`.
- Keyword reference: `/docs/gitlab-ci/yaml/_index.md`.

## GitHub Actions

```yaml
name: CI
on: [push, pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y ninja-build
      - run: cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
      - run: cmake --build build
      - run: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
```

- Several compilers or versions: `strategy: matrix: compiler: [gcc, clang]`.
- Syntax reference: `/docs/github-actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax.md`.

---
name: Docker
description: Build images and run containers or Compose stacks. Load before any docker or docker compose command.
---

- `docker` and `docker compose` use a separate rootless daemon, host `dind`, not the user's machine. Every command needs user approval: group work into few commands.
- Only `/workspace` is shared with containers, at the same path. Bind mounts must use paths under `/workspace`.
- Do not use `--user`: root in containers is the host user, so created files already belong to them.
- Published ports are reachable at `dind:PORT`, not `localhost`. Example: `curl http://dind:8080`.
- Containers have internet access to pull images. You do not.
- Remove what you started when done: `docker compose down`, `docker rm -f <name>`.
- Docs: ZIM file `/data/devdocs_en_docker.zim`.

---
name: C++ tests and benchmarks
description: Write and run C++ tests (GoogleTest, GMock, Catch2), benchmarks (Google Benchmark) and coverage with CTest.
---

Installed: GoogleTest and GMock 1.16, Catch2 3.7, Google Benchmark 1.9. Use GoogleTest unless the project already uses another framework.

Put the tested code in a library target (`add_library(core ...)`), linked by the application and by the tests.

## GoogleTest

```cmake
find_package(GTest REQUIRED)
enable_testing()
add_executable(tests tests/test_core.cpp)
target_link_libraries(tests PRIVATE core GTest::gtest_main)   # GTest::gmock_main for GMock
include(GoogleTest)
gtest_discover_tests(tests)
```

- `TEST(Suite, Name)`, `TEST_F` with a fixture class, `TEST_P` with `INSTANTIATE_TEST_SUITE_P` for parameters.
- `EXPECT_*` continues after a failure, `ASSERT_*` stops the test. Floats: `EXPECT_NEAR`, `EXPECT_DOUBLE_EQ`.
- Crash expected: `EXPECT_DEATH(statement, "message regex")`.
- GMock: `MOCK_METHOD(int, read, (int fd), (override));` then `EXPECT_CALL(mock, read(3)).WillOnce(Return(1));`

## Catch2 v3

```cmake
find_package(Catch2 3 REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(tests PRIVATE core Catch2::Catch2WithMain)
include(Catch)
catch_discover_tests(tests)
```

## Run

```bash
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
ctest --test-dir build -R 'Suite\.' --output-on-failure      # filter by name
ctest --test-dir build --repeat until-fail:50 -R Name        # flaky test
./build/tests --gtest_filter='Suite.*' --gtest_shuffle --gtest_repeat=10
```

## Benchmarks

```cmake
find_package(benchmark REQUIRED)
add_executable(bench bench/bench_core.cpp)
target_link_libraries(bench PRIVATE core benchmark::benchmark_main)
```

```cpp
#include <benchmark/benchmark.h>

static void BM_Parse(benchmark::State& state) {
    const std::string input(state.range(0), 'a');
    for (auto _ : state)
        benchmark::DoNotOptimize(parse(input));
}
BENCHMARK(BM_Parse)->Range(64, 64 << 10);
```

- Always in a Release build. For a comparison, run several times: `./build/bench --benchmark_repetitions=5 --benchmark_report_aggregates_only=true`.
- Report the numbers before and after, from the same machine.

## Coverage

```bash
cmake -S . -B build-cov -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=--coverage -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=--coverage
cmake --build build-cov && ctest --test-dir build-cov
gcovr --root . --exclude tests/ --exclude build-cov/ build-cov
```

## Docs

Markdown in `/docs/googletest` (`primer.md`, `gmock_for_dummies.md`, `advanced.md`) and `/docs/benchmark` (`user_guide.md`).

name: Diagrams
description: Timing diagrams, register maps, frame layouts, PlantUML, Graphviz or D2 diagrams, rendered to SVG or PNG with Kroki. For Mermaid, use the mermaid skill.
---

Write the diagram in a text file, then render it with Kroki:

```bash
curl -sS --fail-with-body --data-binary @timing.json -o timing.svg http://kroki:8000/wavedrom/svg || head -c 1000 timing.svg
```

If the command fails, the output file contains the error: fix the diagram and render again. `png` instead of `svg` for a PNG.

| Need | Kroki type | File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Flowchart, sequence, class, state | `mermaid` | `mermaid` skill |
| Signal timing (SPI, I2C, UART, GPIO) | `wavedrom` | `.json` |
| Register bit fields | `wavedrom` | `.json` |
| Frame or packet layout in bytes | `bytefield` | `.edn` |
| UML when the project already uses PlantUML | `plantuml` | `.puml` |
| Dependency graphs, generated graphs | `graphviz` | `.dot` |
| Architecture with nested boxes | `d2` | `.d2` |

## Examples

Signal timing:

```json
{ signal: [
  { name: "clk",  wave: "p......." },
  { name: "cs",   wave: "10....1." },
  { name: "mosi", wave: "x.345x..", data: ["cmd", "addr", "data"] }
]}
```

Register, bit 0 first:

```json
{ reg: [
  { bits: 1, name: "EN" },
  { bits: 3, name: "MODE" },
  { bits: 4 },
  { bits: 8, name: "DIV" }
]}
```

Frame, one box per byte:

```clojure
(draw-column-headers)
(draw-box "SOF")
(draw-box "LEN")
(draw-box "Payload" {:span 12})
(draw-box "CRC16" {:span 2})
```

name: Documents (PDF, datasheets)
description: Read a PDF, datasheet, reference manual, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, HTML or image file. Converts it to Markdown with Docling first.
---

Never read a PDF or Office file directly. Convert it to Markdown with Docling, 10 pages at a time, next to the original. Give each conversion command a shell `timeout` of 600000:

```bash
curl -sS --fail-with-body -F files=@datasheet.pdf -F page_range=1 -F page_range=10 -F md_compact_tables=true \
  http://docling:5001/v1/convert/file | jq -r .document.md_content > datasheet-p1-10.md
```

Then search the Markdown instead of reading it all: `rg -n -i 'keyword' datasheet-p1-10.md`, then read only the matching part.

## Rules

- 10 pages take about 1 minute. Pages 1 to 10 usually hold the summary, the pinout, the absolute maximum ratings and the table of contents: convert them first, then only the pages you need (`page_range=31`, `page_range=40`...).
- A conversion that timed out keeps running in Docling and delays the next ones: never send the same command again, use a smaller page range.
- Same command, without `page_range`, for `.docx`, `.pptx`, `.xlsx`, `.html` and images. Scanned pages are read with OCR.
- Tables become Markdown tables. Figures become `<!-- image -->`: pinouts, timing diagrams and graphs drawn as pictures are lost. Say so instead of guessing their content.
- Empty file: check the response with `jq '.status, .errors'` instead of `jq -r .document.md_content`.
- Never write into `/docs`: it is read-only.

--- name: Mermaid description: Write Mermaid diagrams (flowchart, sequence, class, state, ER, Gantt) in Markdown files or as SVG/PNG images, and check their syntax. --- GitHub and GitLab display ```` ```mermaid ```` blocks of Markdown files: in a README or a doc, put the diagram there, not an image. For an image, write a `.mmd` file and render it. Always check the syntax by rendering, also for a Markdown block (copy it into a temporary `.mmd` file): ```bash curl -sS --fail-with-body --data-binary @diagram.mmd -o diagram.svg http://kroki:8000/mermaid/svg || head -c 1000 diagram.svg ``` On error, the output file contains the message and the line: fix the diagram and render again. `png` instead of `svg` for a PNG. ## Choose the type | Need | First line | | --- | --- | | Steps, decisions, architecture, data flow | `flowchart TD` (top-down) or `flowchart LR` (left-right) | | Messages between components, protocols | `sequenceDiagram` | | Classes and their relations | `classDiagram` | | State machine | `stateDiagram-v2` | | Database tables | `erDiagram` | | Planning | `gantt` | ## Syntax traps - A node named `end` in lowercase breaks a flowchart: use `End` or `done`. - Quote text containing `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}` or `|`: `A["read (file)"]`, `A -->|"call f(x)"| B`. - `<` and `>` disappear from flowchart labels: write `#lt;` and `#gt;`, as in `A["std::vector#lt;int#gt;"]`. - `;` breaks a sequence message: write `#59;`. - Line break in a text: `
`. - Generics in a class diagram: `class Buffer~T~`, `std::vector~int~ data`. - Short node ids made of letters, digits and `_`, with the text as label: `parser["JSON parser"]`. - No colors or styles unless asked. ## Examples ```mermaid flowchart LR sensor["Sensor (I2C)"] --> mcu[MCU] mcu -->|"UART 115200"| pc[PC] mcu --> err{"Error?"} err -->|yes| led[Red LED] ``` ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant M as MCU participant S as Sensor M->>S: read register 0x0F S-->>M: 0x33 alt no answer after 10 ms M->>M: retry 3 times end ``` ## Docs Mermaid 12.3, one file per diagram type in `/docs/mermaid`: `flowchart.md`, `sequenceDiagram.md`, `classDiagram.md`, `stateDiagram.md`, `entityRelationshipDiagram.md`, `gantt.md`...

name: OpenCV
description: Image processing and computer vision with OpenCV, in C++ or Python (cv2).
---

OpenCV 4.10 with the contrib modules, for C++ and Python 3.

```cmake
find_package(OpenCV REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE ${OpenCV_LIBS})
```

- There is no display: never use `imshow` or `waitKey`. Save results with `cv::imwrite` and check them by values in tests.
- No sample images: create test images in code (`cv::Mat::zeros`, `cv::circle`, `cv::putText`) or ask the user for files.
- `cv::imread` returns an empty `Mat` on failure: check `img.empty()`. Channel order is BGR.
- `cv::Mat` copies share pixels: use `clone()` for an independent copy.
- Python: `import cv2` and `numpy` with the system `python3` (see `python` skill). Images are numpy arrays `(height, width, channels)`.

## Docs

Tutorials in `/docs/opencv/tutorials` (C++) and `/docs/opencv/py_tutorials` (Python). Exact signatures: headers in `/usr/include/opencv4/opencv2/`.

---
name: Protocol Buffers
description: Use Protocol Buffers in C++ or Python (protoc, libprotobuf), or in C for microcontrollers (nanopb).
---

Installed: protobuf 3.21 (`protoc`, C++ library, Python module) and nanopb 0.4.9. Write `.proto` files in `proto3` syntax.

## C++

```cmake
find_package(Protobuf REQUIRED)
add_library(proto proto/msg.proto)
target_link_libraries(proto PUBLIC protobuf::libprotobuf)
target_include_directories(proto PUBLIC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR})
protobuf_generate(TARGET proto)
```

Include `"proto/msg.pb.h"`. `msg.SerializeToString(&bytes)`, `msg.ParseFromString(bytes)` (check the returned bool).

## Python

`protoc --python_out=. msg.proto`, then `import msg_pb2`; `msg_pb2.Point.FromString(data)`, `msg.SerializeToString()`.

## nanopb (C, no dynamic allocation)

Fix the size of strings and repeated fields in a `.options` file next to the `.proto` (same name), otherwise they become callbacks:

```
Point.name max_size:16
Point.values max_count:4
```

```cmake
find_package(nanopb CONFIG REQUIRED)
add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT msg.pb.c msg.pb.h
    COMMAND nanopb_generator -D ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR} msg.proto
    DEPENDS proto/msg.proto proto/msg.options
    WORKING_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/proto)
add_executable(app main.c ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/msg.pb.c)
target_include_directories(app PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR})
target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE nanopb::protobuf-nanopb-static)
```

```c
uint8_t buf[Point_size];
Point p = Point_init_zero;
pb_ostream_t os = pb_ostream_from_buffer(buf, sizeof buf);
if (!pb_encode(&os, Point_fields, &p)) { /* PB_GET_ERROR(&os) */ }

Point q = Point_init_zero;
pb_istream_t is = pb_istream_from_buffer(buf, os.bytes_written);
if (!pb_decode(&is, Point_fields, &q)) { /* PB_GET_ERROR(&is) */ }
```

The library installed here is for the PC. A microcontroller project compiles nanopb's `pb_common.c`, `pb_encode.c` and `pb_decode.c` itself.

## Docs

`/docs/protobuf` (`programming-guides/proto3.md`, `reference/cpp/`, `reference/python/`) and `/docs/nanopb` (`concepts.md`, `reference.md`).

name: Python
description: Write, test, format, and type-check Python 3 scripts and packages.
---

Python 3.13. No internet: `pip install` fails. Installed: pytest, numpy, black, mypy, OpenCV (`cv2`), protobuf.

- Virtual environment that keeps the installed packages: `python3 -m venv --system-site-packages .venv`.
- Scripts: `#!/usr/bin/env python3`, a `main()` called under `if __name__ == "__main__":`, `argparse` for options, `pathlib` for paths, `subprocess.run([...], check=True)` for commands.
- Tests: `python3 -m pytest -q`, in `test_*.py` files with plain `assert`. Useful fixtures: `tmp_path`, `monkeypatch`, `capsys`; parameters with `@pytest.mark.parametrize`.
- Format: `black .`. Types: `mypy --strict file.py` on new code.
- Dependencies: list them in `pyproject.toml` or `requirements.txt`, but only use what is installed here.

## Docs

ZIM files `/data/devdocs_en_python.zim`, `/data/devdocs_en_pytest.zim`, `/data/devdocs_en_numpy.zim`.

---
name: Qt 6
description: Build and test Qt 6 applications (Widgets or QML/Qt Quick) with CMake. Load for any Qt or QML task.
---

- Qt 6.8.2. Modules: Core, Gui, Widgets, Network, Sql, Xml, Concurrent, DBus, PrintSupport, OpenGL, OpenGLWidgets, Test, Qml, Quick, QuickControls2, QuickWidgets, QuickTest, WebSockets, SerialPort, SerialBus, LinguistTools.
- There is no display: `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen` is set. Apps run without a window. Test behavior with Qt Test, not by looking at the UI.
- Connect with pointers to members: `connect(button, &QPushButton::clicked, this, &MainWindow::save);`

## Widgets

```cmake
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.21)
project(app LANGUAGES CXX)
find_package(Qt6 REQUIRED COMPONENTS Widgets)
qt_standard_project_setup()
qt_add_executable(app main.cpp mainwindow.cpp mainwindow.h)
target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE Qt6::Widgets)
```

## QML

```cmake
find_package(Qt6 REQUIRED COMPONENTS Quick)
qt_standard_project_setup(REQUIRES 6.5)
qt_add_executable(app main.cpp)
qt_add_qml_module(app URI App QML_FILES Main.qml SOURCES backend.h backend.cpp)
target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE Qt6::Quick)
```

- Load it in `main.cpp` with `engine.loadFromModule("App", "Main");`.
- C++ type usable in QML: a `QObject` subclass with `Q_OBJECT` and `QML_ELEMENT`, listed in `SOURCES`. Properties: `Q_PROPERTY(int count READ count NOTIFY countChanged)`. Methods called from QML: `Q_INVOKABLE`.
- Check QML files with `cmake --build build --target all_qmllint`: it knows the project's modules, unlike `qmllint` alone. Format them with `/usr/lib/qt6/bin/qmlformat -i Main.qml`.

## Tests

C++ (Qt Test):

```cmake
find_package(Qt6 REQUIRED COMPONENTS Test)
enable_testing()
qt_add_executable(tst_foo tst_foo.cpp)
target_link_libraries(tst_foo PRIVATE Qt6::Test)
add_test(NAME tst_foo COMMAND tst_foo)
```

A test file ends with `QTEST_MAIN(TestClass)` and `#include "tst_foo.moc"`. Signals: `QSignalSpy spy(obj, &Obj::changed); QCOMPARE(spy.count(), 1);`

QML (Qt Quick Test), with `tst_*.qml` files next to the CMakeLists.txt:

```cmake
find_package(Qt6 REQUIRED COMPONENTS QuickTest)
qt_add_executable(tst_qml tst_qml.cpp)
target_link_libraries(tst_qml PRIVATE Qt6::QuickTest)
target_compile_definitions(tst_qml PRIVATE QUICK_TEST_SOURCE_DIR="${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}")
add_test(NAME tst_qml COMMAND tst_qml)
```

`tst_qml.cpp` contains `#include <QtQuickTest>` and `QUICK_TEST_MAIN(qml)`. A test file:

```qml
import QtQuick
import QtTest

TestCase {
    name: "Math"
    function test_add() { compare(1 + 1, 2) }
}
```

# Infrastructure

_Open source, decentralized and self-hosted infrastructure for many local services and authentication with Authelia._

## Features

- [x] caddy 2 HTTP/S reverse proxy
- [x] Authelia (SSO / authentication middleware)
- [x] local_ai: Ollama (ROCm), Open WebUI, OpenCode, VS Code server, Kiwix, Docling, Kroki, Speaches (voice)
- [x] Compiler Explorer
- [x] qbittorrent and transmission (Torrent client/server)
- [x] Docker / docker-compose
- [x] Homepage (Dashboard)
- [x] SearXNG (Self-hosted search engine)
- [x] Jellyfin (Eg Netflix, Disney+)
- [x] Forgejo (Git server, fork of Gitea)
- [x] Uptime Kuma (Monitoring)
- [x] Argus (Application update monitoring)
- [x] SyncThing (File synchronization)
- [x] Dufs (File server)
- [x] PsiTransfer, ProjectSend, Picoshare (File sharing)
- [x] it-tools, omni-tools and cyberchef (Tools for IT)
- [x] Privatebin
- [x] Memos (Note-taking)
- [x] Stirling PDF (PDF tools)
- [x] Wordpress (Via FASTCGI/caddy)
- [x] Dependency-Track (SBOM / vulnerability tracking)
- [X] Game (Satisfactory, Minecraft, 7 Days to Die, Team Fortress 2 etc...)

### Clone

Clone this repository to your local machine using:

```sh
git clone --recurse-submodules --remote-submodules https://github.com/bensuperpc/infrastructure.git
```

Go to the folder

```sh
cd infrastructure
```

### Start the infrastructure

```sh
make init
```

Build the local images (opencode, vscode-server, compiler-explorer), before the first start and after changing [images/dev](infrastructure/images/dev/Dockerfile):

```sh
make build
```

Start the website with:

```sh
make up
```

Stop the website with:

```sh
make stop
```

Remove containers with:

```sh
make down
```

Services are enabled via **preset configuration files** in the [`presets/`](presets/) directory. 

The active presets are declared in the [`Makefile`](Makefile) via the `CONFIGS` variable, for example, `CONFIGS := local_ai` loads `presets/local_ai.conf` which activates the `main_infrastructure`, `caddy`, `homepage` and `local_ai` profiles. It can also be set for one command: `make CONFIGS="local_ai tools" up`.

The domain and the certificates are set once, in [infrastructure/.env](infrastructure/.env.example) (created by `make init`):

```sh
DOMAIN=bensuperpc.org

LISTEN_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0
```

For local testing:

```sh
DOMAIN=bensuperpc.localhost
TLS=internal
LISTEN_ADDRESS=127.0.0.1
```

### Configure the infrastructure

Every secret is in one file, `infrastructure/.env` (gitignored), created by `make init` from [.env.example](infrastructure/.env.example): each `__GENERATE__` becomes a random value. 

The services' `<name>.env` files, next to their compose file, are tracked in git and hold no secret: they read them as `${NAME}`, e.g. `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://litellm:${LITELLM_DB_PASSWORD}@litellm-postgres:5432/litellm`, so a database and its client share the same value.

#### Authelia - user database

`make init` writes `infrastructure/services/infra/authelia/config/users_database.yml` (gitignored) with one admin, from `AUTHELIA_ADMIN_USER`, `AUTHELIA_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `AUTHELIA_ADMIN_PASSWORD` in `infrastructure/.env`, if the file does not exist yet. To change the password or add users, edit the file with an argon2 hash:

```sh
docker run --rm authelia/authelia:4.39.28 authelia crypto hash generate argon2 --password 'MyPassword'
```

After 5 wrong passwords in 3 minutes, Authelia refuses logins for 30 minutes.

#### Dozzle - user account

Generate a user entry for [users.yml](infrastructure/services/infra/dozzle/config/users.yml):

```sh
docker run -it --rm amir20/dozzle generate bensuperpc --password mypassword --email bensuperpc@gmail.com --name "bensuperpc"
```

#### OpenSSH - public key

Replace [id_ed25519.pub](infrastructure/services/infra/openssh/config/authorized_keys/id_ed25519.pub) with your own public SSH key.

#### local_ai

The `local_ai` profile runs a local AI stack that works offline once downloaded (about 20 GB), it needs an AMD GPU (ROCm, `/dev/kfd` and `/dev/dri`), an NVIDIA GPU or Intel GPU.

| Service | Role | First access |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open WebUI | Chat, RAG, voice | The first account created is admin |
| OpenCode | Coding agent with offline docs (Kiwix) | `docker exec opencode opencode pair --url https://opencode.<DOMAIN>` |
| VS Code server | Editor | Password: `VSCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` |
| LiteLLM | Proxy for external APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic...) | `litellm.<DOMAIN>`, `admin` / `LITELLM_UI_PASSWORD` |
| Ollama | Local models (`OLLAMA_MODEL`, `EMBEDDING_MODEL`) | - |
| Speaches | Speech to text and text to speech (CPU) | - |
| vLLM | Hugging Face models (`VLLM_MODEL`), optional `vllm` profile | Add it in LiteLLM, see below |

Open WebUI and OpenCode have no direct internet access: web search goes through SearXNG, limited to the domains in [whitelist.txt](infrastructure/services/ai/searxng/config/whitelist.txt).

To add models (Ollama library or Hugging Face GGUF):

```bash
docker exec ollama ollama pull qwen3.8:27b
docker exec ollama ollama pull nomic-embed-text-v2-moe # Mandatory embedding model
docker exec ollama ollama pull gemma4:12b
docker exec ollama ollama pull qwen3.5:9b
docker exec ollama ollama pull hf.co/<author>/<repo>:<quant>
```

#### Team Fortress 2 - Steam GSLT

`make init` will remind you: set `TEAMFORTRESS2_SRCDS_TOKEN` in `infrastructure/.env` with your token from [steamcommunity.com/dev/managegameservers](https://steamcommunity.com/dev/managegameservers).

#### Dependency-Track - first login

Default credentials are `admin` / `admin` - **change them on first login**.

#### Argus - GitHub token

Argus checks about 30 GitHub projects every hour, within GitHub's 60 requests per hour without a token. For more, set `ARGUS_GITHUB_TOKEN` in `infrastructure/.env` with a fine-grained token without any permission.

#### Forgejo - installation

On the first start, `git.<DOMAIN>` shows the installation wizard, filled in from [forgejo.env](infrastructure/services/dev/forgejo/forgejo.env): create the administrator account there. The wizard writes `INSTALL_LOCK = true` to Forgejo's `app.ini`: do not set `FORGEJO__security__INSTALL_LOCK` in `forgejo.env`, Forgejo applies the `FORGEJO__*` variables at every start and `false` would break the installation.

### Homepage

You can change the homepage config in these files:

- [bookmarks.yaml](infrastructure/services/infra/homepage/config/bookmarks.yaml)
- [services.yaml](infrastructure/services/infra/homepage/config/services.yaml)
- [settings.yaml](infrastructure/services/infra/homepage/config/settings.yaml)
- [widgets.yaml](infrastructure/services/infra/homepage/config/widgets.yaml)

### Forgejo Runner

The `forgejo` preset starts a runner, registered without any manual step:

- `forgejo_runner_register` waits for the end of the installation wizard, registers the runner in Forgejo with `FORGEJO_RUNNER_SECRET` (generated by `make init`), then exits.
- `forgejo_runner` then starts with [runner.yml](infrastructure/services/dev/forgejo/config/runner.yml).

Labels for `runs-on:`: `docker` (Node 22), `ubuntu-latest`, `ubuntu-24.04` and `ubuntu-22.04` (`ghcr.io/catthehacker/ubuntu` images). Edit them in `runner.yml`, then `docker restart forgejo_runner`.

`actions/checkout` and the other actions are downloaded from `https://data.forgejo.org`. Jobs reach Forgejo directly at `http://forgejo:3000`, without Authelia.

### Docker volumes

This infrastructure uses docker volumes to store data, all configuration/data for each service are not shared between services for security and maintenance reasons, but **public_data** and **private_data** are shared between all services to store your data.

| Volume name  | Description                                                                                                |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| public_data  | Public data reachable on internet via [dufs.bensuperpc.org](https://dufs.bensuperpc.org), can be disabled. |
| private_data | Private data                                                                                               |

### SSH access

The default port for SSH/rsync is 2222.

You can access to the server with:

```sh
ssh -p 2222 admin@bensuperpc.org
```

### Qbittorrent

To activate the alternative webui theme (VueTorrent), you need to go in the qbittorrent settings, then in the `webui` section, check the `Use alternative webui` and add `/vuetorrent` to text field.


### Local testing

Set in `infrastructure/.env`:

```sh
DOMAIN=bensuperpc.localhost
TLS=internal
LISTEN_ADDRESS=127.0.0.1
```

`*.localhost` names resolve to 127.0.0.1 without `/etc/hosts`, and Caddy signs the certificates with its own CA, so Authelia works as online, after the first start, import Caddy's root certificate in your browser:

```sh
make caddy-root
```

Variables exported in your shell (`DOMAIN`, `OLLAMA_MODEL`...) take precedence over `infrastructure/.env`: unset them before `make`.
